headline: 24-YEAR HIGH IN TREASURY YIELDS EASES — GOLD RECOVERS TO $4,140 AS BOND MARKET TESTS GENERATIONAL INFLECTION
snippet: US Treasury yields briefly hit their highest level in 24 years on October 8 before partially retreating, allowing physical gold to recover to $4,140 per ounce. USAGold's daily market report flagged the milestone as a potential inflection point — the bond market's 'higher for longer' thesis either cements or breaks here, a pivot that will directly set gold's trajectory into year-end with the Fed keeping December as a live meeting.

headline: SPANISH MOUNTAIN GOLD DRILLS 295.5M AT 0.54 G/T — NEAR-SURFACE EXPANSION FILLS BC FEASIBILITY PIT SHELL
snippet: Spanish Mountain Gold (TSXV: SPAU) reported drill hole 26-DH-1414 returning 295.5 metres averaging 0.54 g/t gold from 41 metres depth at its BC deposit, expanding near-surface mineralization within the open pit shell targeted in the company's 2028 Feasibility Study. The broad, shallow intercept strengthens the resource block model underpinning the strip ratio and capital efficiency assumptions as the 60,000-metre feasibility drill program continues.

headline: RECORD SEASON COMPLETE: ALASKA SILVER WRAPS ILLINOIS CREEK — ASSAYS PENDING ON 21M OZ WATERPUMP CREEK
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Alaska Silver (TSXV: WAM)
snippet: Alaska Silver (TSXV: WAM) wrapped its record-setting 2026 summer drill program at Illinois Creek, Alaska, targeting two high-priority zones: the Waterpump Creek high-grade deposit (21.4 million inferred ounces silver at 279 g/t) and the newly identified Silver Sage discovery that returned 148 g/t Ag over 4.4 metres in 2025. The program grew mid-season after a C$7.6 million financing and marks the most aggressive summer in company history; first assays are expected in coming weeks.

headline: CARLIN GOLD LOCKS ROYALTIES ON SNOWLINE GOLD AND FIREWEED ZINC — YUKON'S TWO FLAGSHIP PLAYS IN ONE ROYCO
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Carlin Gold (TSXV: CGD)
snippet: Carlin Gold (TSXV: CGD) announced royalty positions on two of Canada's most actively drilled exploration names — Snowline Gold's Valley porphyry deposit in Yukon's Rackla Gold Belt and Fireweed Metals' Macmillan Pass zinc district. The announcement positions Carlin as an emerging micro-cap royalty aggregator with leveraged exposure to resource milestones at both properties without requiring additional capital for exploration.

headline: ENERGY FUELS DOWN 8% OCTOBER 7, OFF 33% YTD — URANIUM-RARE EARTH HYBRID FACES EXECUTION CREDIBILITY TEST
snippet: Energy Fuels (TSX: EFR) fell 8.27% on October 7 and is now down 33% year-to-date as investors grow impatient with the timeline gap between the company's dual uranium-rare earth strategy and actual earnings contribution from its Australian Strategic Materials acquisition. Unlike peer USA Rare Earth and MP Materials — which fell on geopolitical thaw — Energy Fuels' slide is driven by specific execution uncertainty around integrating a rare earth metals and alloys processing platform while managing core uranium production.

headline: CLEANTECH LITHIUM OPTIONS TWO NEW ANTOFALLA BRINE BLOCKS — CONSOLIDATES ARGENTINA FOOTPRINT NEAR LAGUNA VERDE
snippet: CleanTech Lithium (AIM: CTL) secured options on two lithium brine properties in Argentina's Salar de Antofalla, adjacent to its flagship Laguna Verde project, consolidating a contiguous position across one of South America's highest-priority lithium brine corridors. The additions let CleanTech advance regional exploration without diluting the core Laguna Verde development timeline as the company works toward a definitive feasibility study.

headline: GOLD-SILVER RATIO WIDENS TO 70X — SMM CONFIRMS DIVERGENCE DEEPENING AS INDUSTRIAL DEMAND LAGS MONETARY BID
snippet: Shanghai Metals Market's October 9 morning review confirmed the gold-silver divergence that started October 7 is deepening, with spot gold stabilizing at $4,133.63 while silver lagged at $59.17 — pushing the gold-to-silver ratio to approximately 70x. SMM analysts attribute the pattern to silver's greater sensitivity to industrial demand uncertainty from rising bond yields and softened Chinese post-Golden Week restocking, while gold's monetary demand holds the floor above $4,100.
